Subgroup-level hazard ratios

Source: R/group_analysis_summary.R
group_analysis_summary.Rd

Compute the number of patients, the log hazard ratio, and its standard error in each level of each subgroup variable of a patient-level dataset.

Usage

group_analysis_summary(
  patient,
  variables = setdiff(colnames(patient), c("treatment", "time", "event"))
)

Arguments

patient

Patient-level survival data with subgroup columns, usually the output of group_sample_unconstrained(), group_sample_constrained(), group_optimize_unconstrained(), or group_optimize_constrained(). Must have the columns of the output of group_data_patient() and the subgroup columns named in variables.

variables

Character vector of unique names of subgroup columns in patient. Each subgroup column must be character or factor with no missing values. Defaults to every column of patient other than treatment, time, and event.

Value

A tibble in the format of the output of group_data_summary(), with one row per subgroup level, ordered by subgroup variable as in variables and then by level, and the following columns:

  • variable: character, name of the subgroup variable.

  • level: character, level of the subgroup variable.

  • patients: integer, number of patients in the subgroup level.

  • log_hazard_ratio: numeric, estimated log hazard ratio of treatment versus control in the subgroup level.

  • standard_error: numeric, standard error of the log hazard ratio.

Details

For each level of each subgroup variable, group_analysis_summary() fits a Cox proportional hazards model by partial likelihood to the patients in that level, with treatment as the only covariate and the Efron method for ties, as in survival::coxph(). The log hazard ratio is the estimated coefficient of treatment versus control, and the standard error is on the log hazard ratio scale. These are the observed statistics \(\hat\beta_k(x)\) and \(\hat\sigma_k(x)\) of the "Loss function" section of vignette("optimization", package = "retrogroup").

If the model cannot be fit for some subgroup level, for example because one of its arms has no patients or no events, the log_hazard_ratio and standard_error of that level are NA.

The levels of a factor subgroup column are its factor levels, in order, excluding levels with no patients. The levels of a character subgroup column are its sorted unique values.

See also

Other analysis: group_analysis_probability()

Examples

  patient <- group_data_patient(
    group_example_patient(),
    arm = "arm",
    treatment = "Lev+5FU",
    time = "time",
    event = "event"
  )
  summary <- group_data_summary(
    group_example_summary(),
    variable = "variable",
    level = "level",
    patients = "patients",
    log_hazard_ratio = "log_hazard_ratio",
    standard_error = "standard_error"
  )
  set.seed(0)
  sample <- group_sample_constrained(patient, summary)
  group_analysis_summary(sample)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   variable level      patients log_hazard_ratio standard_error
#>   <chr>    <chr>         <int>            <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 age      under 60        280           -0.198          0.174
#> 2 age      60 or over      339           -0.517          0.163
#> 3 node4    no              453           -0.291          0.139
#> 4 node4    yes             166           -0.587          0.230
#> 5 sex      female          312           -0.188          0.160
#> 6 sex      male            307           -0.587          0.179
  summary
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
